name: Von Restorff Effect
description: An item that stands out from surrounding similar items is remembered better than the others.
design_relevance_note: Commonly cited to justify highlighting a single CTA button — worth using with the nuance below rather than the raw 'stand out = memorable' shorthand.
myth_risk_note: Multiple converging sources (behavioral, neurophysiological, and cross-cultural replication) back the effect with no disputing paper found in this discovery pass, but no dedicated meta-analysis was found either -- rated low rather than none since the evidence base, while consistent, is narrower than a fully meta-analyzed claim would warrant.
prevalence_note: Known in visual-design circles under the 'isolation effect' framing for highlighting a single CTA or item, less universally cited than the foundational-tier laws.

findings.description: A genuinely distinctive/isolated item within a list is better remembered than surrounding items, but the effect depends specifically on relative distinctiveness within the list's context, not on raw perceptual salience alone — a more nuanced finding than the popularized 'stand out visually and people will remember it' shorthand often used in design.
findings.source_title: The subtlety of distinctiveness: What von Restorff really did

applications.title: A text-note-styled ad standing out in a photo-dominated social feed
applications.description: An advertisement formatted to look like a plain text note (mimicking the Apple Notes visual style) stood out and captured attention specifically because it broke from the photo-based visual convention of the social media feed surrounding it, illustrating that distinctiveness relative to context, not intrinsic quality, is what makes something memorable.
applications.ethical_note: A pure visual-attention mechanism with no deceptive framing -- standing out via format contrast doesn't misrepresent the ad's content, so this carries no persuasion-ethics dimension beyond ordinary advertising.
